note: Trainable: eligible for the fine-tune query distribution.

queries.query: Agrippa's opening claim that reality is layered into three realms of matter, heavens, and pure mind, and that the magician draws power down from each level into the one beneath
queries.note: The three-fold world of Book I ch. 1-2; 'Elementary, Celestial and Intellectual' and 'collect virtues' paraphrased into plainer words; 'Agrippa' kept as the author any reader knows.

queries.query: how to recognize which planet rules a given stone, herb, or animal, and why the eagle, the rooster that greets the dawn, and gold all answer to the Sun
queries.note: The Solary correspondences of ch. 23; 'Solary', 'queen of birds', 'imitation of their rays' paraphrased away; eagle/rooster/gold kept as reader-honest emblems of the doctrine.

queries.query: why meeting a bewitcher's gaze was thought dangerous: an emanation bred from the purest blood streams out through the eyes and seizes another person's spirit
queries.note: Fascination in ch. 50; 'lucid subtile vapor', 'heat of the heart', 'binding' paraphrased away.

queries.query: stories of imagination reshaping the flesh, like a man who could bring paralysis on himself at will and another who went mad by acting madness too convincingly
queries.note: The passions changing the body by imitation, ch. 64; 'palsy', 'phantasy', and the names Avicen and Gallus Vibius paraphrased away (not names a general reader carries).

queries.query: can spoken words carry real power to change the world
queries.note: The occult virtue of words and charms in ch. 69-71; mantra, dhikr, and creative speech traditions all answer this. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: what can dreams reveal about things that have not yet happened
queries.note: Divination by dreams in ch. 59; dream oracles are pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.
